study.title: Effect of Acupuncture in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer Disease: A Functional MRI Study
study.study_design: single block experimental design, within-subject fMRI study with three conditions (resting state, acupuncture stimulation, post-acupuncture resting state), three groups (MCI, AD, healthy controls)
study.blinding: fMRI post-processing was performed by a single experienced observer, unaware to whom the scans belonged
study.population: Thirty-six right-handed subjects (8 MCI patients, 14 AD patients, and 14 healthy elders)
study.disease_condition: Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer Disease (AD)
study.inclusion_criteria: AD: complete physical and neurological examination, standard laboratory tests, extensive neuropsychological assessments; diagnosis fulfilled DSM-IV criteria for dementia and NINCDS-ADRDA criteria for possible or probable AD; CDR of 1 and 2. MCI: impaired memory performance on normalized objective verbal memory test; recent history of symptomatic worsening in memory; normal or near-normal performance on global cognitive tests (MMSE score >24), as well as on activities of daily living scale; global rating of 0.5 on CDR Scale, with score of at least 0.5 on memory domain; absence of dementia. Healthy controls: no neurological or psychiatric disorders such as stroke, depression and epilepsy; no neurological deficiencies such as visual or hearing loss; no abnormal findings such as infarction or focal lesion in conventional brain MR imaging; no cognitive complaints; MMSE score of 28 or higher; CDR score of 0. All subjects were right-handed.
study.exclusion_criteria: Participants with contraindications for MRI such as pacemaker, cardiac defibrillator, implanted material with electric or magnetic system, vascular clips or mechanical heart valve, cochlear implant or claustrophobia were excluded. In addition, patients with a history of stroke, psychiatric diseases, drug abuse, severe hypertension, systematic diseases and intellectual disability were excluded.

interventions.procedure_label_exact: acupuncture stimulation on the acupoints of Tai chong and Hegu
acupoints_used_exact: Tai chong (Liv3) on the dorsum of the left and right foot
He gu (LI4) on the dorsum of the left and right hand
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: dorsum of the left and right foot (Tai chong/Liv3); dorsum of the left and right hand (He gu/LI4)
interventions.needle_size_exact: 0.30 mm in diameter and 25 mm long
interventions.needle_retention_exact: 3 minutes (during fMRI acquisition); needle withdrawn after 3 minutes
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: hold still, keep eyes closed and think nothing in particular
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: acupuncture at Tai chong (Liv3) and He gu (LI4)

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sensory/deqi responses during acupuncture were not measured or reported in this study.

neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: echo-planar imaging (EPI); repetition time (TR)/echo time (TE)/flip angle (FA)/field of view (FOV) = 2000 ms/40 ms/90°/24 cm, image matrix = 64×64, slice number = 33, thickness = 3 mm, gap = 1 mm, bandwidth = 2232 Hz/pixel. 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient echo (MPRAGE) sagittal images: TR/TE/inversion time (TI)/FA = 1900 ms/2.2 ms/900 ms/9°, image matrix = 256×256, slice number = 176, thickness = 1 mm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: resting state: 3 minutes; acupuncture stimulation: 3 minutes; post-acupuncture resting state: 10 minutes
neuroimaging_methods.preprocessing_software_exact: statistical parametric mapping (SPM8) software (Wellcome Department of Imaging Science; http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm)
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: MNI (Montreal Neurological Institute) space by normalizing with the EPI template via their corresponding mean image
neuroimaging_methods.smoothing_exact: Gaussian kernel of 8 mm full width at half-maximum (FWHM)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: All participants had less than 3 mm of translation in x, y, or z axis and 1° of rotation in each axis
statistical_thresholds_exact: voxel-level height threshold of p<0.001 (uncorrected) and a cluster-extent threshold of 5 voxels

Table 2 labels 'AD vs. NOR' results only show decreased activity rows. No increased activity rows are listed for AD vs. NOR in the table, consistent with the results text. This has been faithfully extracted.

The contrast design is described as two-sample t-tests comparing patient groups vs. normal controls within each condition/timepoint contrast. The exact GLM contrast weights are not fully specified beyond the block design description. The contrasts for 'acupuncture vs. baseline' and 'post-acupuncture rest vs. baseline' are within-subject first-level contrasts carried forward to between-group second-level t-tests.
Table 6 row 'Rt. Middle Temporal Gyrus' has x=-66 which appears to be Left hemisphere based on sign, but the table labels it 'Rt.' This is copied exactly as reported in the paper.
Table 6 row 'Lt. Parahippocampa Gyrus' has Brodmann area listed as '35-' (with trailing dash). This has been preserved exactly as printed in the paper.

The total number of volumes (317) is mentioned in preprocessing: 'a mean image was created over the 317 realigned volumes.' This corresponds to the 3+3+10=16 minutes of total scanning, but the calculation of 317 volumes at TR=2000ms does not perfectly match 16 minutes (960 seconds = 480 volumes). This inconsistency is present in the paper and has not been resolved.

The n_analyzed values for contrast entries were derived from the sum of the two groups being compared (e.g., 8 MCI + 14 NOR = 22 for MCI vs. NOR contrasts; 14 AD + 14 NOR = 28 for AD vs. NOR contrasts), as the paper does not explicitly state per-contrast sample sizes. This is an inferred value.
No information on deqi needle sensation, needle depth achieved, or patient-reported responses to needling is provided.

Table 5 (MCI after acupuncture vs. resting state, decreased) has a row 'Lt. Superior Frontal Gyrus' with BA=18 and coordinates 18, -100, -11. BA 18 does not anatomically correspond to Superior Frontal Gyrus. This is copied exactly as printed in the paper.
